questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design progressive delivery gates at scale, with multi-cloud constraints and real-world SLO-based rollouts; focuses on policy, tooling (Argo Rollouts, Prometheus), and CI integration; evaluates trade-offs between safety and speed, failure modes; ensures observability and reproducibility.

## Key Concepts

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for promotion failure modes if the AnalysisTemplate temporarily becomes unavailable?
- How would you adapt this gate for multi-tenant environments with separate SLIs per tenant?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml

      - name: predictor
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

```yaml
      cpu: 100m

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 300"]
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod in test namespace (tries to access prod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "wget http://prod.svc.cluster.local || true"]
```

```yaml
# DNS test Pod (for compliance with DNS allow rule)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"]
```

## Follow-up Steps
- kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
- kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml; kubectl exec compliant-pod -- curl logs.internal:443
- kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml; observe failure to reach prod
- Check events: kubectl describe networkpolicy/test-egress-isolate -n test

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CI gating, SBOM generation, and license compliance in a mono-repo.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- SPDX license checks and whitelisting
- Per-service CI gates in a mono-repo
- Interpreting SBOM/license failures

## Code Example
```yaml
name: SBOM and License Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          echo "build service image"
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft image:myorg/service:sha -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Upload SBOM
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sbom.json
          path: sbom.json
```

## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up

- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

## Code Example
```python
# manifestlint.py
import yaml, sys
ALLOWED_NS = {"dev","staging","prod"}
ALLOWED_REG = {"registry.trusted"}

def ok(manifest):
  docs = yaml.safe_load_all(manifest)
  for m in docs or []:
    if m.get("kind") in {"Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet"}:
      ns = m.get("metadata", {}).get("namespace")
      if ns not in ALLOWED_NS:
        return False
      for c in m.get("spec", {}).get("template", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", []):
        img = c.get("image", "")
        if not any(img.startswith(r) for r in ALLOWED_REG) or ":latest" in img:
          return False
  return True

if __name__ == '__main__':
  path = sys.argv[1]
  with open(path) as f:
    print(ok(f.read()))
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly
